info.title: Recommenditos used-car price API
info.description:
Estimates the asking price of a used car in the eight countries of the
AutoScout24 data, with the model the service was built with.

Every error is an RFC 9457 Problem Details object (`application/problem+json`);
a 422 lists every invalid field in `errors`. See `docs/docs/api.md` in the
repository for how to run the service and how errors are shaped.

post.summary: Find real listings comparable to a used car described in part
post.description:
Up to `k` listings of the training and validation data like the car (FR-09).

The body is `/v1/price-range`'s plus `k` (5 by default, at most 20), and it
is checked the same way (FR-03, FR-04). A listing is comparable when it has
the car's `make` and `model`, its age differs by at most 2 years and its
mileage by at most 25 %; the closest mileage comes first, then the closest
age. A field the request leaves out sets no filter, and no filter is ever
relaxed, so a car outside every window gets an empty list. A service built
without the index answers 503. Every answer is one record of the prediction
log (FR-13); when it cannot be written, the answer is a 503.

422.description: The request is invalid; `errors` lists every invalid field.

errors.detail: 'Trabant' is not a make the served model supports.
Input should be less than or equal to 1200

413.description: The body is larger than 10 KB (NFR-09).

example.title: Content Too Large
example.detail: The request body is larger than the limit of 10240 bytes.

post.summary: Estimate the asking price of a used car
post.description:
Values one listing with the served model.

The ten required fields are those of FR-01; every other field is optional,
and an omitted one reaches the model as absent. A make the model does not
support is refused with a 422 that lists the supported ones (FR-04). A
model name or a country the training data does not hold is accepted and
reported in `warnings` (FR-05).

The `explanation` says where the estimate starts and which five fields move
it most, each as a percentage, so a client can check the estimate (FR-08).
Every answer is one record of the prediction log (FR-13); when it cannot
be written, the answer is a 503. A price that is not a finite number is a
500 and is neither answered nor logged.

post.summary: Estimate the price range of a used car described in part
post.description:
The nominal 90 % price range of a car, and its typical price (FR-07).

Only `make` is required (FR-02): any other field may be left out, and the
range widens the less the request says. Every field that is given is
checked as `/v1/predict` checks it (FR-03, FR-04), and an unseen `model` or
country is answered and reported in `warnings` (FR-05). The typical price is
the one `/v1/predict` gives when the request carries all of its required
fields, and the range's median otherwise; the bounds always contain it. A
bundle without interval models, such as `lgbm-extended`, answers 503.
Every answer is one record of the prediction log (FR-13); when it cannot
be written, the answer is a 503 too.

get.summary: Service status, the served model and the comparables index
get.description:
Answers `ok` whenever the service is up, with the model and the index it serves.

The model and the comparables index are loaded before the service accepts
its first request, so a service that answers here can value a listing.
`price_range` says whether it can also answer `/v1/price-range`, which needs
interval models the bundle may not carry, and `comparables` names the index
`/v1/comparables` searches, or is null when the service has none.

get.summary: Service name, served model and documentation links
get.description:
The landing page of the service, for a person who opens its address.

Links are relative to the service, so they hold behind a reverse proxy.

get.summary: Request, latency, error and model metrics for Prometheus
get.description:
Every metric of the service, summed over its worker processes.

For Prometheus to scrape inside the deployment: the reverse proxy refuses
this path from outside. `docs/docs/api.md` lists the metrics.

# TYPE http_requests_total counter

http_requests_total{method="POST",path="/v1/predict",status="422"} 3.0

base_price_eur.title: Base Price Eur
base_price_eur.description: Where every estimate starts before any field moves it, in EUR: the model's average log price over its training listings, as a price.

top_features.title: Top Features
top_features.description: The five fields with the largest effect, largest first, whether it raises or lowers the estimate. Equal effects keep the order of the request body; a model that reads fewer than five fields lists all of them.

other_features_effect_pct.title: Other Features Effect Pct
other_features_effect_pct.description: The combined effect of every field the model reads that `top_features` does not list, in percent; 0 when there is none.

Explanation.title: Explanation
Explanation.description:
Why the estimate is what it is: where it starts and what moves it (FR-08).

The effects multiply: `base_price_eur` times `1 + effect_pct / 100` over the
entries of `top_features` and `other_features_effect_pct` gives the estimate.

field.title: Field
field.description: The request field, as the request body names it. Every model feature is attributed to the field it comes from: `registration_date` covers the car's age, and an equipment list covers all of its items together.

effect_pct.title: Effect Pct
effect_pct.description: The field's multiplicative effect on the estimate in percent: `12.5` raises it by 12.5 %, `-30` lowers it by 30 %. It is `exp(φ) - 1`, where φ is the field's SHAP value on the model's log price scale.

FeatureEffect.title: FeatureEffect
FeatureEffect.description: How much one request field moves the estimate (FR-08).

ValuationRequest.title: ValuationRequest
ValuationRequest.description:
One listing to value (UC1): the ten fields FR-01 requires, the rest optional.

The optional fields are the inputs of the basic and the extended feature set.
The served model reads the ones its feature set holds and ignores the rest,
so a model trained on another set needs no change here (FR-12).
